item.title: On-Device Age Verification and Squarespace Unicode Phishing Bypass
item.content:encoded:
The Squarespace Phish With No Brand Text to Match — Should Read

A Squarespace phishing email bypassed brand-text detection by hiding the brand name with invisible Unicode characters and placing it only inside an image, while passing SPF, DKIM, and DMARC through a hijacked aged domain. It was ultimately caught through behavioral signals such as malicious link reputation, sender anomalies, and OCR/image-based detection.

  • A credential-harvesting email impersonating Squarespace reached a K-12 school district and used a fake billing notice to warn that a domain would be deactivated in two days.
  • The word “Squarespace” did not appear as machine-readable text in the message because the logo and wordmark were delivered as an image and the subject and sender display name were padded with invisible U+206E characters.
  • The message passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC because it was sent from the hijacked 24-year-old domain oldanopetroli[.]com through Aliyun DirectMail infrastructure.
  • The payment link led to a tokenized subdomain on compromised studiointech[.]net, which was flagged malicious.
  • IRONSCALES Themis flagged the incident at 90% confidence as Credential Theft and Image-Based Attack and automatically resolved it as phishing before anyone in the district acted on it.

The Future of Age Verification: Your Face Never Leaves Your Device — Optional

Incode is promoting on-device age estimation that verifies a user’s age locally on their phone, tablet, or laptop so facial images are not transmitted or stored. The company argues this privacy-by-architecture approach helps platforms meet expanding age-verification laws while reducing biometric data exposure and fraud risk.

  • Incode says more than 30 age assurance laws are now in force worldwide, including the UK Online Safety Act, Australia’s under-16 rules, Brazil’s Digital ECA, and age verification mandates in about half of U.S. states.
  • Incode’s On-Device Age Estimation runs facial age estimation and passive liveness detection on the user’s phone, tablet, or laptop so the face is not transmitted or stored.
  • The system sends only the age-threshold outcome onward, while a server-side layer analyzes session metadata to detect injection attacks, tampering, and other session integrity issues without facial or biometric information.
  • Incode says it compressed its facial age estimation and passive liveness models to roughly one-tenth of their original size using knowledge distillation so they can run in ordinary browsers or apps without special hardware.
  • Incode announced a $100 million commitment to privacy-preserving identity infrastructure alongside its acquisition of Identiq, whose technology is intended to let organizations share fraud signals without exposing customer data to a third party.
